extra.message: Remote Code Execution via eval in patient_formula_cast_256 — An attacker can execute arbitrary system commands, fully compromising the server, accessing sensitive data, and pivoting to internal networks. [verified: The 'expr' GET parameter is passed directly to eval() at line 80 without any sanitization. The gate _wrk_gate only checks authentication, not the input content; with empty __builtins__, classic subclass traversal still enables full code execution.]

Weak Default SECRET_KEY in settings.py — An attacker can forge session cookies, CSRF tokens, password reset tokens, and other signed data, potentially leading to account takeover and unauthorized access. [verified: The SECRET_KEY defaults to the weak hardcoded value 'dev-only-change-me' when DJANGO_SECRET_KEY is unset (line 6). This key is used by Django for signing sessions, CSRF tokens, and password reset tokens; an attacker knowing this default can forge all signed data, leading to session hijacking and account takeover.]

Debug Mode Enabled by Default in settings.py — An attacker can trigger errors to obtain sensitive information (e.g., file paths, database credentials, internal IPs), aiding further attacks. [verified: DEBUG defaults to True when DJANGO_DEBUG env var is unset, allowing detailed error pages that leak sensitive configuration and source code; no compensating controls such as custom error handlers or production overrides exist in the displayed code.]

Patient IDOR in Appointment Creation — A patient can create an appointment on behalf of any other patient, potentially interfering with provider schedules and viewing other patients' information in related workflows. [verified: The AppointmentForm sets a filtered queryset on the patient field but does not override clean_patient to enforce that the submitted patient belongs to the current actor. Since hidden widgets and queryset restrictions are client-side only, a patient can submit a crafted POST with an arbitrary patient ID, bypassing the intended restriction.]

Open Redirect in patient_return_lane_155 — An attacker can redirect users to malicious sites, aiding phishing attacks or credential theft. [verified: The 'lane' parameter from GET/POST (line 66) is passed directly to Django's redirect() without any validation, allowing an attacker to supply an external URL (e.g., https://evil.com) and trigger an open redirect. The _wrk_gate check only restricts access to authenticated workers but does not sanitize the redirect target.]
